hall.line: A long room, and the far end of it is not lit.

look.say: The stone is worn low down the middle, a band two strides wide. It runs from the steps to the dark.

study.say: The mark cut into the door is the mark cut into the stone. Your thumb has it before your eyes do.

study.refuse: Something is cut into the door, deep and worn shallow. Your thumb goes over it and takes nothing.

objects.name: a door at the end of the room

listen.say: It does not move and it does not breathe. It holds the cold the way the pool held the water.

shore.line: Grey water, and no far side to it.

study.say: The stone is warm where nothing else is. A mark is cut into the top of it, deep enough to read with your thumb.

read.say: The marks hold still. They are names in a line, all walking the same way.

read.refuse: The marks swim. You cannot hold them.

objects.name: a book, face up in the shingle

look.say: The pool is shallow and clear. Your face does not arrive in it.

listen.say: You hold still and listen. There is your breath, and the water, and nothing under either.

follow.say: The path climbs off the shingle and inland. It runs the way the names run in the book.

follow.refuse: The path goes up into the dark. You have no name for what is at the top of it.

stair.line: The steps go up inside the rock, and the cold comes down them.

climb.say: You go up. The turn is always the same turn, and then the steps stop.

touch.say: Cut stone, wet under the hand. It is rubbed smooth at the height of a shoulder, the whole way up.

listen.say: Cold comes down the steps and goes out behind you to the water. Nothing comes down with it.
